How much of the sailing you do is up to you. Rent a bareboat and skipper it yourself if you hold a recognised licence such as the ICC or RYA Day Skipper. Prefer to relax? Add a professional skipper to any yacht at checkout — they know the local winds, the moorings and the taverns no guidebook lists. And for a pure floating-villa holiday, choose a crewed yacht where the skipper and hostess handle everything from cooking to route planning.
Sailing yacht, catamaran or motor yacht

Monohull sailing yachts give the purest feel of the wind and the best value per berth. Catamarans have become the family favourite: no heeling, two hulls of private cabins and a saloon the whole crew fits into. Motor yachts trade sails for speed and cover twice the miles in a day, while traditional gulets pair a professional crew with the romance of wooden decks. Every listing on ▪▪▪▪▫▪▪▪ shows cabins, berths, build year and the obligatory extras before you commit.
Where and when to set sail

The Mediterranean season runs from April to October: July and August bring guaranteed sun and the liveliest harbours, while May, June and September offer warm seas, steadier winds and noticeably lower prices. From November to April the fleet moves to winter waters — the Caribbean, the Bahamas and the Seychelles sail at their best while Europe waits for spring. Most charters run Saturday to Saturday from well-connected home marinas, so flights and transfers are easy to plan.

Pick your destination and dates, browse available yachts, and click Reserve on the boat you like. We confirm availability with the partner, send a booking proposal, and once you pay the deposit your charter is locked in. The whole flow takes a few minutes.

For bareboat charter (without skipper) you need a sailing licence recognised by the country of charter — a Croatian boat licence, RYA Day Skipper, ICC, or equivalent. If you do not have a licence you can still book any yacht and add a skipper at checkout.

The base rate covers the yacht itself, standard equipment, charter agency support and insurance against major damage. End cleaning, fuel, mooring fees outside the home marina, transit log and tourist tax are usually paid separately — every yacht detail page lists the obligatory and optional extras transparently.

Yes. Bareboat charter is available on most yachts in our catalogue, provided at least one person on board holds a valid sailing licence and a VHF radio licence. If no one in the group has a licence, you can rent the same yacht with a professional skipper for an additional daily fee.

May, June and September are the sweet spot — warm sea, light winds, fewer crowds and noticeably lower prices than peak July and August. April and October still work for confident sailors who do not mind a cooler sea, and they offer the lowest weekly rates of the year.

Cancellation policies vary by yacht — every offer page shows the exact terms before you pay. Within ▫▫ hours of booking you can cancel free of charge with a full refund; after that the operator's terms apply, so we recommend travel insurance that covers trip cancellation. Refundable security deposit is always returned unless the yacht is damaged.
